modes.name: Prose wall
modes.definition: A section carries list-like or multi-point content as a paragraph instead of bullets, a numbered list or a diagram.
modes.include: Paragraphs of 3+ sentences holding separable points; text the reviewer called hard to scan or eye-glazing.
modes.exclude: A 1-2 sentence lead-in to a list or diagram. Content that should be deleted outright is low-signal-content.

modes.name: File map not first
modes.definition: The Solution tab does not open with the file tree or a diagram; prose comes before the reader's mental map.
modes.include: A file tree that exists but sits below approach prose; no file tree or diagram at all.
modes.exclude: A one-line heading or caption above the file tree.

modes.name: Implementer-level detail
modes.definition: The plan does the implementer's job: full function or test bodies, or line-by-line edit recipes, instead of seams, public signatures and brief comments.
modes.include: Complete test functions; complete function bodies; step-by-step edit instructions ('before calling X, check for Y').
modes.exclude: Signatures, interface changes and pseudo-code sketches. A snippet that is itself the entire change on a very small task.

modes.name: Low-signal content
modes.definition: The plan contains at least one passage that can be deleted without losing anything a reader needs.
modes.include: Filler lead-ins ('Two small changes:'); statements of the obvious ('tests use Vitest'); restating repo facts or other parts of the doc; long passages that reduce to 'extend the existing pattern at [path]'.
modes.exclude: Needed content that is badly formatted (prose-wall).

modes.name: Open questions untagged
modes.definition: Open questions or assumptions that need human attention are written as prose or checklists instead of the built-in open-question element.
modes.include: 'Assumptions (comfortable proceeding on): ...' lists in prose or checkboxes.
modes.exclude: Decisions the plan resolves itself and does not ask a human to confirm.

modes.name: Given/When/Then rendered inline
modes.definition: Given/When/Then clauses of a scenario render as one run-on line instead of one clause per line.
modes.include: Clauses on separate source lines but without list markers or line breaks, so they collapse into one paragraph when rendered.
modes.exclude: Clauses rendered one per line (bullets or explicit breaks), whether or not the labels are aligned.
